claim: Warfarin and aspirin together increase bleeding risk.

evidence.text: Concomitant use of warfarin and aspirin significantly increases bleeding risk.

claim: Clarithromycin is contraindicated with simvastatin.

evidence.text: Simvastatin is contraindicated with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors like clarithromycin.

label: SUPPORTED

claim: Calcium carbonate decreases levothyroxine bioavailability.

evidence.text: Calcium carbonate reduces gastrointestinal absorption of oral levothyroxine.

label: SUPPORTED

claim: Ciprofloxacin elevates theophylline concentration.

evidence.text: Ciprofloxacin reduces the clearance of theophylline, leading to elevated serum concentrations.

label: SUPPORTED

claim: Grapefruit juice increases atorvastatin plasma levels.

evidence.text: Consumption of grapefruit juice raises plasma concentrations of atorvastatin.

label: SUPPORTED

claim: Ketoconazole inhibits the metabolism of cyclosporine.

evidence.text: Ketoconazole is a potent inhibitor of CYP3A and increases blood levels of cyclosporine.

label: SUPPORTED

claim: Aspirin completely prevents bleeding when taken with warfarin.

evidence.text: Aspirin added to warfarin increases the risk of major hemorrhages and bleeding complications.

claim: Simvastatin is completely safe with erythromycin at high doses.

evidence.text: Co-administration of erythromycin with high doses of simvastatin causes severe myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.

claim: Metformin combined with contrast media has no risk of lactic acidosis.

evidence.text: Intravascular administration of iodinated contrast materials during metformin therapy can lead to acute renal failure and lactic acidosis.

claim: Oral contraceptives maintain normal clearance when combined with ampicillin.

evidence.text: Ampicillin has been reported in rare cases to reduce oral contraceptive efficacy.
Clinical pharmacology evaluations demonstrate no systematic reduction of steroid hormone levels with ampicillin.

label: CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE

claim: Ginkgo biloba combined with anticoagulants causes unpredictable bleeding changes.

evidence.text: Some case reports suggest Ginkgo biloba increases bleeding risk with warfarin.
Controlled trials observed no significant change in INR or bleeding times when Ginkgo biloba was added to warfarin.
